reason: While the passage narrates Jonathan's steadfast loyalty and generosity toward David (demonstrated through his covenant, gift of royal possessions, and defense against Saul's jealous persecution), it does not present a model of 'good leadership characterized by humility in the face of criticism.' The text does not depict Jonathan humbly accepting criticism, but rather courageously standing by his friend against unjust persecution. When Jonathan confronts his father's murderous rage, he responds by leaving in anger (וַיָּ֞קָם יְה֣וֹנָתָ֔ן מֵעִ֥ם הַשֻּׁלְחָ֖ן בָּחֳרִי־ אָ֑ף - 'he rose from the table in burning anger'), not with humble acceptance. The passage emphasizes personal loyalty and courageous friendship rather than a leadership model responding humbly to criticism.
